summary: Feed s178_triple is degraded with 3 active faults: 17.1 Gbps bursts overloading 10 Gbps NDR port (171%), 19.0% frames sliced to 192 bytes removing payload, and 98.9% encrypted traffic exceeding 90% NDR tolerance. All reduce NDR detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Almost all traffic (98.9%) is TLS/encrypted and is being forwarded as-is with no decryption/visibility zone before the NDR. Packet broker has no SSL visibility or selective decrypt policy, so NDR receives opaque payloads.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR is blind to payload content - cannot do deep inspection, JA3, certificate analysis, or detect malware/C2 inside encryption. Exceeds NDR's 90% encrypted tolerance, severely limiting detection coverage to metadata only.

recommended_fix.why: NDR needs cleartext payload for detection; decrypting relevant traffic (or feeding decrypted copy) restores visibility while staying within privacy policy. Do not decrypt blindly - use selective policy.

findings.root_cause: Single 10 Gbps NDR port is fed bursty aggregate traffic peaking at 17.10 Gbps in 1ms intervals (171% of capacity). No load-balancing or aggregation shaping on packet broker; bursts directly hit tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR will drop packets at ingress during bursts, causing missed flows, incomplete TCP reassembly, and missed detections. Sustained overload also risks tool crash or backpressure.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 2+ NDR ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port load <80% and preserve both directions of each flow for NDR state tracking.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen is enabled and truncating frames to ~192 bytes (1399/7351 frames = 19.0% truncated). Likely configured to save bandwidth/tool load but incompatible with this NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload (tool profile: needs_full_payload=true) for signature matching, file extraction, and anomaly detection. Sliced frames lose L7 payload, causing false negatives and broken reassembly.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing or set snaplen to NDR max 9216 bytes so full payload is delivered; use filtering or load-balancing instead of slicing to handle overload.
